question: Two banks, A and B, offered loans at 3.5% and 7% per annum, respectively. Ashish borrowed an amount of ₹4,40,000 from each bank. Find the positive difference (in ₹) between the amounts of simple interest paid to the two banks by Ashish after 4 years.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Same principal and time ⇒ difference depends only on rate difference

Rate difference = 7 − 3.5 = 3.5%

SI difference = 440000 × 3.5% × 4

= 440000 × 0.035 × 4

**∴ Difference = 61600**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Principal = 440000, Time = 4 years

Rates = 3.5% and 7%

**Formula used:**

Simple Interest = (P × R × T) / 100

**Calculation:**

⇒ SI₁ = (440000 × 3.5 × 4) / 100 = 61600

⇒ SI₂ = (440000 × 7 × 4) / 100 = 123200

⇒ Difference = 123200 − 61600 = 61600

**∴ The correct answer is ₹61600.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Simple Interest Formula

SI = (P × R × T) / 100

Rate Difference Trick

If P and T are same, SI difference = P × (R₁ − R₂) × T / 100

Unit Consistency

Always use same time units (years here) for SI calculations
